title: Identical scenario_value_stats / scenario_value_histogram inline parsers duplicated across parseOptimiserSolveResult and parseFrontierSelectResponse
description: The inline object literal that validates `scenario_value_stats` (11 fields: mean/std/min/max/p5/p25/p50/p75/p95/pct_increase/pct_decrease, each via expectNumber) is written out verbatim twice: once in parseOptimiserSolveResult (lines 1480-1490) and once in parseFrontierSelectResponse (lines 1540-1550). The `scenario_value_histogram` inline parser (counts + edges, each `parseArray(... expectNumber ...)`) is likewise duplicated (lines 1492-1497 and 1552-1557). The two copies differ ONLY by the parser-name string literal ('parseOptimiserStatusResponse' vs 'parseFrontierSelectResponse'). Both blocks already operate on a pre-resolved `stats` / `histogram` value produced by optionalNullableObject(...) and both target the same shared wire types (OptimiserScenarioValueStats / OptimiserScenarioValueHistogram in api/types.ts:624-641), so there is no shape difference justifying the copy.
evidence: guards.ts:1480 `mean: expectNumber("parseOptimiserStatusResponse", stats.mean, "field \`scenario_value_stats.mean\`")` is identical to guards.ts:1540 `mean: expectNumber("parseFrontierSelectResponse", stats.mean, "field \`scenario_value_stats.mean\`")` for all 11 fields; the histogram blocks at 1495-1496 and 1555-1556 are identical save the parser name. Both `stats` values come from optionalNullableObject (1457, 1521) and both types alias the same OptimiserScenarioValueStats/OptimiserScenarioValueHistogram interfaces.
est_reduction: ~30 lines (two 11-line stats blocks collapse to one helper call each; two histogram blocks likewise)
behavior_preservation: Extract `parseScenarioValueStats(parser: string, stats: Record<string,unknown>)` and `parseScenarioValueHistogram(parser: string, hist: Record<string,unknown>)` taking the parser-name as a parameter, then call them with the existing literals. Field paths (e.g. `field \`scenario_value_stats.mean\``, `field \`scenario_value_histogram.edges\``) and parser prefixes are reproduced byte-for-byte, so all loud-failure error messages are unchanged. Contract tests assert on `scenario_value_histogram.edges` / `.counts` (guards.contract.test.ts:1026,1039) which the parameterized helper preserves exactly; no behavior change.
